Former Goldberg Synagogue

Former Synagogue · Goldberg, Germany

Goldberg's synagogue was built in 1845 as a substantial brick building with a gabled roof and round-arched windows at today's Jungfernstraße 34. Jewish worship ceased after the First World War, although an exact closure date is not verified. In 1925 the Roman Catholic Church acquired the building and adapted it for Christian worship. The original synagogue therefore survives in altered form but no longer serves a Jewish religious function. A plaque at the property recalls its former role. No exact inauguration year is entered because the available heritage source specifies the building year rather than an opening ceremony.
